observed.initial_blocker: OP_CALL used recursive Python self._call(...), making host Python recursion depth an implicit ClayVM call-depth/failure semantic.

grf.hypothesis: A VM-owned explicit activation-frame stack with a ClayVM-owned frame limit removes Python recursion depth from Clay call semantics without changing the admitted bytecode contract.
grf.counterhypothesis: Replacing host recursion with explicit frames changes return propagation, argument isolation, resource-limit behavior, or existing arithmetic/process semantics.
grf.discriminator: Retain existing regressions, require an explicit ClayVM frame-depth trap, and execute a call chain deeper than the deliberately lowered Python recursion limit.

ordinary_regressions: prior function-order semantic twin retained as ordinary regression

exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.intervention: Temporarily lower Python sys recursion limit to 500 inside a local disposable test, then compare a recursive Python depth-1200 baseline against a 1200-deep Clay call chain executed with explicit VM frames; restore the original recursion limit in finally.
exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.baseline_result: Python recursive baseline raised RecursionError as predicted.
exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.candidate_result: Explicit-frame ClayVM returned integer 7 for the 1200-deep Clay call chain.
exactly_one_bounded_unusual_experiment.rollback: Original Python recursion limit restored; disposable local candidate only.
